review_material.assessment: The source provides a complete derivation of the flight-size PDF for two regimes: constant pore length and exponentially distributed pore length, both with constant diving rate. These regimes share the same control (flight distance x) and readout (flight-size PDF p(x)), and each yields a quantitative exponential decay law with a characteristic length. The cluster is supported by the supplement lines 370-443. The main-text model (variable diving rate, Gamma-distributed pore lengths) is not selected per the routing hint. The extracted evidence supports a numeric control (x), a numeric readout (p(x)), a quantitative mechanism (exponential decay), and an objective response within an explicit domain, so case_authoring_ready is true.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper develops an alternated continuous-time random walk (A-CTRW) model for colloid filtration in a heterogeneous porous medium, linking pore-scale flight-dive dynamics to macroscopic deposition profiles and breakthrough curves. The supplement derives the flight-size PDF under different pore-length and diving-rate assumptions. The selected cluster focuses on the two constant-diving-rate regimes: constant pore length and exponentially distributed pore length.
